about: US answer key rule changes and what each one touches (Brandon t915u, Nov 9 2026 4:40 PM CST; KZ4CP 5:12 PM CST). This file is part of the US rules hash. A rules change rebuilds ONLY the declared states; a park with saved record ids keeps its result through it (kpc_us_key.py) unless the change sets saved_ids: true. One entry per change, newest last: id, when, why, from (the US rules hash it moves FROM: the hash of the last build), scope = {states: ['US-TN', ...], saved_ids: false} or 'all' (every state: only when the change really touches every state). An undeclared change rebuilds the whole key (safe default). Emergency full rebuild by hand: the 'states' input 'all'. Nov 9 evening (KZ4CP 5:41 PM CST): a scope may also list park refs, 'parks': ['US-1234', ...]: only those parks are re-matched (their states are read again, every other park there keeps its result). A scope that lists nothing means ALL; a change that touches no park says scope 'none'.

changes.why: PAD-US load fix (Brandon 11:24 AM CST): saved ids always loaded by id, the state layer before the PAD-US name exception. It changes what every state reads, so every state is rebuilt once; parks with saved ids keep their result.
Bad-ID block list (Brandon t919u; the list is empty) + parks with saved ids keep their result through rule changes (Brandon t915u) + this scope file. Changes no current result.

State GIS paging honors the layer maxRecordCount so a silent server page cap is not treated as the last page, and a short layer already in the saved copy is re-read. It changes what every state may read from a state layer.

A saved copy the master gate holds is refilled first (KPC_REFILL_ONLY: saved PAD-US ids by id and the newer or short state layers, then the same gate again); a re-read that comes back with fewer records than the saved layer no longer replaces it; and every services*.arcgis.com host (services2 to services9 too) is saved-copy only on every path. What a state may read live changes, so every state is rebuilt once.

The master step (before the gate) is now the one writer of the saved copies: the key reads short or new layers into layer files for it (KPC_LAYER_OUT), reads a person's checked download instead of the live layer (KPC_LAYER_IN), and the build only reads the saved copies (KPC_MASTER_OWNS). services-<region>.arcgis.com hosts (services-eu1 and the like) count as services*.arcgis.com, and ncnhde.natureserve.org is never contacted (saved copy only). What a state may read live changes, so every state is rebuilt once.

changes.why: Fresh-start run 42891101784 held FL, UT and DE. The live layer count is now a plain returnCountOnly query: with page and outline parameters, one server counted a single page window (FL DEP state-owned lands 188 of 77,144), one capped the count at the page (NRHP 200), and one refused it (DE state lands). The layer file counts with this state's own entry of a prefix (its where), not the first one. When a short page without exceededTransferLimit leaves records in the state box unread (a server that cuts the row window before the box), the read steps through the layer window by window. What a state reads changes, so every state is rebuilt once.
changes.restamped: 2026-11-10: the layer count and the layer read now follow redirects only through the master step's checked opener (every hop: saved-copy-only and never-contact hosts, the host rule, then robots.txt); same scope. APPROVED, decided_by KPC owner, 2026-11-10. Re-stamped again 2026-11-10: every live read of the US key (PAD-US get and fields, resolve, zip_state, the layer count and read) goes through that checked opener, and the first address, each hop and each hop's robots.txt are paced 2 s per host (kpc_host_pace); same scope. APPROVED, decided_by KPC owner, 2026-11-10

changes.why: Review fixes to the readers. Every layer read is whole or it fails: the read asks the layer's own count and record ids with the same where and box, reads by id, and never keeps a partial layer (the window paging assumed the server's window size and could stop short). PAD-US has the same count check and the same per-layer time limit. One Vermont layer was listed twice and read twice; a layer listed under two prefixes is read once. A park left with no record is graded pin, not official. Host rules come from the one shared guard. Any state layer or PAD-US read could have been cut, so the scope is all.

Florida's state box now takes in the Keys and the Dry Tortugas (kpc-us-states.json draws Florida without them, south edge 25.12): FL DEP state-owned lands sent 77,144 of 79,689 records, the 2,545 left out all in Monroe County. Every live layer of one state also writes the layer's own total (no box) into its layer file as count_layer, so the master step can refuse a box read that leaves records of the layer out (layer files only, no join changes outside Florida). Only Florida's box changes.
changes.restamped: 2026-11-11 r2 (Quality NO on #126): count_layer is written only for a layer whose every key entry is this one state's (NRHP and the USACE layer are listed once per state, and their unboxed total is the whole country), and it is always written for such a layer, None when the count fails, so the master step holds that read; same scope (US-FL). APPROVED, decided_by KPC owner, 2026-11-10

changes.why: Florida's state box east edge moves from -80.0 to -79.8. Run 43037613117 refused the checked FL DEP state-owned lands hand file (hand-US-FL.sgflf, 79,689 records) because 45 parcels off Miami (lon -79.875 to -79.858) lay east of the box: 79,644 of 79,689, SHORT, not merged, so the saved copy kept its old 77,144. No Bahamas land is inside the new edge (Bimini is at -79.3). Only Florida's box changes.

D6, tables out of the rule scripts (KPC owner, 2026-11-12): BOX_ADD and the agency layers read for listed states only (the state-limited XS entries) move, unchanged, from kpc_us_key.py into data/us-key/area-tables.json, read at start (fail closed on a missing or malformed file); a park's read date falls back to one run date (KPC_BUILD_DATE, else today read once) instead of a per-park clock call. No result changes: the loaded tables equal the old ones (XS in the same order), and the builder gives byte-identical key files before and after on the same saved copy (tests/test_area_tables_nov12.py). So no state is rebuilt for it; an area-hash add run rebuilds every state once (the code hash moved: the D7 switch-over run).

KPC-Links #151 on today's data: data/us-key/overrides.json (1,527,615 bytes, over the 1 MB cap) becomes a manifest (parks with a 'no' list, blocked_ids, the parts list) plus data/us-key/overrides-parks-01.json and -02.json. kpc_us_key.py loads them through kpc_overrides.load, which stops the build on a missing or bad part instead of reading an empty set. The loaded parks and blocked_ids are identical to the single file (5,038 parks, canonical sha256 0dc041b8dc76984b740edab31ca093cad6400c1704284f0e4002a7321c8ac93a). No join rule changes and no key rebuild is required.

Handoff item 5 (key checks at join time; v4 answer 1): a record whose own type field says conservation easement (PAD-US Category/Des_Tp, a state layer's CATEGORY/TYPE/CLASS/INTEREST field, or its source fields): a NEW join by name alone is refused in every state (the piece goes to CHECK with the reason). An EXISTING one (saved record ids kept through a rules change) is not removed; it is listed in data/us-key/review/easement-name-joins.csv (ref, record, state). New York re-checks its existing ones too. A person's join (overrides, reviewed) still stands. Seen in NY: a Conservation Easement record joined to Storm King US-2146 by its name.
changes.scope_note: The US key hash moves, so every US state needs a fresh key build before its next 2-fer run; the owner times this PR. saved_ids false: parks with saved record ids keep them (existing easement joins are listed, not removed), except in New York, which re-checks them in kpc_us_key.py (EASEMENT_RECHECK_STATES).

changes.why: D11 (owner ruling, 17 Nov 2026): data/state-gis.json, the US key's list of state layers, joins the US rules hash (kpc_key_freeze RULE_FILES['us-key']), and every layer in it gets one more field, 'what': owned, designation, water, register or compilation (340 layers; the 131 filed as kind 'land' first: 64 owned, 28 designation, 17 register, 3 water, 19 compilation). Labels and hash in one change, so the hash moves once. No join changes: kpc_us_key.py does not read 'what' (it reads url, nm, kind, water, where, nm2, ag), and the key builder gives the same layer table before and after (tests/test_d11_layer_list_nov17.py). The labels change a join only when a later rule reads them (T5 / D3 / D4), and that rule comes with its own park list.

D1 (owner ruling, 17 Nov 2026): a saved record id is the LAND, not the number. Behind the rule switch KPC_SAVED_ID_LAND (OFF): a park whose saved ids are carried through a rules change keeps a row only while its record still carries the saved name and acres within 10% (20 acres at least); a renumbered row is found again by name + acres in the same layer near the pin; if that fails the old row is not carried and the record goes to check. Switch OFF = no result changes anywhere. Measured offline on Florida's saved copy with the switch ON: 32 parks / 197 rows pointed at other land (one state layer renumbered: Big Shoals State Park 13 of 19 rows, Big Shoals State Forest 12, Andrews WMA 15 ...); all 197 were found again in the same layer, 0 sent to check.

D9 (owner ruling, 17 Nov 2026): one record, one park. Behind the rule switch KPC_ONE_RECORD_ONE_PARK (OFF): a record still joined by name to two or more parks goes to the ONE park whose full name is the record's own name (kpc_key_rules.d9_winner); the others give it back to check. Parks given their own parts of the record (rule B12) and hand joins are never moved; no single winner = left for the tripwire list. Switch OFF = no result changes. Measured on the live US key: 169 shared records would settle, 167 parks give one back, 1 ends as a pin; 911 shared records have no single winner. (The drawn outline now honours the key's B12 part boxes, kpc_outlines_from_key.py, not a rule file.)

D4 + D5 (owner rulings, 17 Nov 2026), each behind its own rule switch (OFF). D4 KPC_LAKE_ONLY_IF_LAKE: a park with land of its own never takes a lake surface by name (only a park whose own type says it is the lake keeps one; a park with no land record keeps its lake for a person). D5 KPC_NO_LEASE_BY_NAME: a leased / agreement / cooperative-area record is never joined by name alone (the easement family). Both act on a park's fresh match, like the easement rule; rows carried through a rules change stay until a park-scoped re-match. Live key (as published): D4 87 parks carry a lake surface beside land of their own (17 water-only parks left for a person); D5 21 name-only joins to a lease / agreement record. Switches OFF = no result changes.

D4 rewritten (owner, 17 Nov 2026 9:17 AM, after the research in d4-research.md: the first D4 decided by the park's KIND and was wrong both ways). Now WHO OWNS THE WATER decides: a lake surface joined by name stays only when the park has land of its own and the lake sits inside that land (kpc_key_rules.lake_inside_land: inside the land's box, no bigger than the land; over 3 times the land never), or the park has no land record and its own type says it is the water (state fishing lake, reservoir). Everything else goes to CHECK for a person (a park on the Corps', Reclamation's or a utility's lake never takes it). Still behind KPC_LAKE_ONLY_IF_LAKE (OFF) = no result changes.

D4 precheck (offline AR / ID / WA build, switches on): a park whose own TYPE is the water (a state fishing lake, a reservoir area) keeps its lake even when it also has a small land record (Liberty Lake, Chambers Lake, Lake Desire State Fishing Lakes in WA had been sent to CHECK). Other parks unchanged: lake inside their land, else CHECK. Switch KPC_LAKE_ONLY_IF_LAKE still OFF.

D4 precheck (AR / ID / WA, saved ids re-matched): a park whose NAME says it is a reservoir's area ('Magic Reservoir BLM Recreation Management Area', 'Anderson Ranch Reservoir Management Area', 'Scooteney Reservoir State Park') keeps its reservoir surface; the research found these areas manage the water. A park named only 'Lake X State Park' is not covered (the lake is often another owner's). Switch KPC_LAKE_ONLY_IF_LAKE still OFF.

D3 (owner ruling 17 Nov 2026, built 10:00 AM), switch KPC_DESIGNATION_SPLIT (OFF): (1) a national heritage area / corridor (a line around mostly other people's land) gets no outline: pin + 'sits on' (the key's new 'on' list names its records); (2) a federal designation line (Forest Service designated areas, BLM monuments / NCAs, FS + BLM wilderness, BLM study areas, a PAD-US Designation record) joined by name is kept only on the park that IS that designation (its name, its name without type words, or the same kind of place); on another kind of park it goes to CHECK. State layers labelled 'designation' wait for D7 (reading D11's labels moves every area's hash). Ownership share (approximate / herd areas on checkerboard) is a report first. Offline precheck UT / AK / GA: 3 heritage areas become pin + sits on; UT 1 park loses 2 neighbouring study-area pieces (Black Ridge Canyons West).

Reviewer B #7 (owner 17 Nov: stick to Fable's plan; step 0): the rule switches are read from .github/key-switches.json per state (an environment variable still wins), the file is a US rule file sliced per state in the area hash (a state with no switch on gets no part), and a key rules / switch file that cannot load stops the build instead of turning every rule off. Every switch is OFF in the file: no result changes.

THE CONTEST (matching plan section 1, Fable; owner YES 17 Nov 12:25 PM), behind KPC_ONE_RECORD_ONE_PARK with D9 (OFF): a record joined by name to two or more parks goes to the park it fits best (full name, then the record's own type words incl. short forms SP / SF / WA / WMA / SB / SHP / SRA / SNA / DNP / NWR / NF, then the layer's kind, then place words); a record naming both kinds stays on both; a tie or a bare name leaves every park for a person; and exact name wins: a record whose full name is another park of the state goes back from the park that took it. Hand joins and B12 parts are never moved. Offline proof OH / WI / MD / NE: 37 / 1 / 11 / 15 parks change, none becomes a pin (two same-name POTA numbers keep a shared record); the bare-name records sent to a person are Ohio's basemap copies ('CAESAR CREEK'), the parks keep their division layers' records.

Handoff 8 part 2 (US fixes 1-4: Park Service unit codes, Forest Service river names + second name, R-G8 other kinds of place, measured acres) + D1 on a person's own rows in overrides.json (KPC_SAVED_ID_LAND: a join or NO whose record now holds other land moves to the same name + acres in the same layer; a join not found again stays and goes to check). Every switch OFF: no result changes.

Scorecard finding: the id-join name test (KPC_ID_JOIN_NAME) and the D1 saved-row test (KPC_SAVED_ID_LAND) read only a record's first name; Ohio's first name is a code ('CaesarCrkSP'), so 164 Ohio hand joins failed with KPC_ID_JOIN_NAME on. Both now accept any of the record's names (second name, and the key's shown 'second (first)'). Both switches OFF: no result changes.

HQ key batch 2 (Fable's matching plan): KPC_AGENCY_TIE (the contest asks the agency of each park's POTA website, from .github/key-agency-table.json learned from the person-reviewed joins, before a 'person' answer), KPC_STATE_COPY (D7: a record from a layer D11 labels 'compilation' goes to check beside the agency's own record, or grades the park approximate alone), D3 also reads D11's 'designation' label (under KPC_DESIGNATION_SPLIT). 'what' is now read by the US key, so a US state's state-gis.json slice keeps its labels (Canada's still leaves them out). Every switch OFF: no join changes.

Scorecard finding: KPC_STATE_COPY (D7) took 56 hand-picked Tennessee state parks off their TDEC 'compilation' layer (TDEC's public lands hold TDEC's own parks). D7 now acts only on a park whose POTA website is a federal agency's (its ruling's case, a state copy of a federal unit): the copy goes to check beside a federal record, or grades the park approximate alone. Switch OFF: no result changes.

The owner's go (17 Nov 7:10 PM, 'go for what you want'): the eleven key rules built today are switched ON for the eight states the scorecard tested (AR, DE, GA, MD, MI, OH, RI, TN): KPC_NPS_UNIT_CODE, KPC_FS_RIVER_NAMES, KPC_G8_OTHER_PLACE, KPC_MEASURED_ACRES, KPC_SAVED_ID_LAND, KPC_ONE_RECORD_ONE_PARK, KPC_DESIGNATION_SPLIT, KPC_LAKE_ONLY_IF_LAKE, KPC_ID_JOIN_NAME, KPC_AGENCY_TIE, KPC_STATE_COPY. Offline grade, all on vs all off, people's answers hidden: FOUND 658 -> 665, WRONG 66 -> 51; one record lost (DE McGinnis Pond, a bare name shared by two parks, now a person's question). Builds stay by hand.

Sonnet's grade of the first new-rule build (MD MI OH TN): (1) KPC_FS_RIVER_NAMES's second-name-field join took Ohio's STATE PARK records into 12 wildlife areas, nature preserves and state forests (Ohio keeps a code first, 'CaesarCrkSP', and the readable name second): a STATE LAYER record's own layer kind must now agree with the park (PAD-US records are not affected, so Ozone Falls SNA keeps its join). (2) KPC_NPS_UNIT_CODE replaced the North Country Trail's official trail line with an 81-acre NPS piece: a trail park keeps its line. Switches on only in the 8 states; offline OH / MI: FOUND unchanged, the 13 wrong joins gone, the trail line back.

changes.why: Q1 (KPC owner 18 Nov 5:48 AM, 'Yes to 1-3'; reading ruled 1:45 PM, 'Go with what you think is best'; key-quality.md sections 11 step 1 and 14): the rows of an approximate saved answer ('reviewed-approx', the closest official land, bigger or another shape) go to check until a person verifies an outline with evidence; rows the rules joined alone stay; a park left with nothing is pin only and its last outline is never kept. Switch KPC_APPROX_PIN, default ON. Parks with an approximate answer are always re-matched, so saved ids need no re-match. The states are every state whose key holds such a park (a park in two states counts in both: Natchez Trace in AL, MS and TN). Fable's round 2: keep-last-good (kept, refound, transferred) takes an approximate park's old reviewed-approx rows out first, so a run whose read misses their land does not bring them back (Split Rock, Jordan Craters, Lake Abert, Devil's Rock Garden).

changes.why: Held states (key-quality.md sections 10 and 11 step 2; causes B + C): (a) a record whose name has no type word takes its kind from its LAYER's title (contest + D3; Gold Butte NM, Red Cliffs NCA; Mount Irish Wilderness no longer takes the ACEC record), a compilation or register layer gives none; (c) a record carrying one sharing park's exact full name in any of its names stays with that park (Lieber SRA); (d) the heritage line is for NATIONAL heritage areas only (Old Ruby State Park State Heritage Area); (e) the designation core name is compared without spaces and 'reserve' is a designation word (Pat's Cabin, Beech Creek); and 'Coastal Reserve' is a reserve type word (Buxton Woods). The contest and D3 run in every state, so every state is rebuilt and saved ids are re-matched. After Fable's review (18 Nov 1:50 PM): a bracket word that differs between sharing parks is part of the name (never same name or same place; a record carrying one park's bracket word goes to it: Horseshoe Canyon (North) / (South)); the US kind tag 'wild' is wilderness, not wildlife; a layer kind that fits none of the parks falls back to the bare-name path (size, agency, then a person). Second round (18 Nov evening): a layer's '(<kind>, state GIS table)' tail is not its title (Kenai River); the contest's size step counts a held record only when its box covers the shared record's box (60%: Big Lake's neighbour 47%, Caddo Lake WMA's own copy 70%), so two neighbours of about the same size are not one piece of land (Big Lake NWR / the state's Big Lake). Last look (Fable, 19 Nov): (b) 'same land' by place name TAKEN OUT (Seven Sisters US-12918 is a 7.8-acre fishing access site beside the WMA); a pair is the same land only when a person recorded it with evidence; the label stays only for the same full name with the same bracket words.

changes.why: R-PP1 (Fable 19 Nov; key-quality.md section 19 items 4 and 10; Brandon 6:04 AM 'use your judgment or maybe outside agent confirm'): a park number does NOT cover the national preserve beside it unless POTA's own name for that number says so. POTA numbers park and preserve apart where it wants them (Glacier Bay US-12607 + US-0029, Aniakchak US-0902 + US-0003, Great Sand Dunes US-0033 + US-8295). A Park Service record named Preserve that the NAME rules joined to a park-only number (Wrangell-St. Elias US-0069, Katmai US-0044, Lake Clark US-0048, Gates of the Arctic US-0026, Craters of the Moon NM US-0665), or a park / monument record joined to a preserve-only number, goes to check. A person's join stands. A combined 'Park and Preserve' or 'Monument and Preserve' name is both (Oregon Caves US-0953 keeps its one record). R-PP1a (Fable 19 Nov, owner 8:13 AM '1 yes for now'): a row whose record holds POTA's OWN PIN for that number stays where it is and is named once in the run's notice as a person's question (Wrangell-St. Elias US-0069 and Craters of the Moon US-0665 keep the preserve until POTA answers; Katmai, Lake Clark and Gates of the Arctic move). R-PP1a as amended (round 3; Fable sitting 3, owner 10:12 AM): the pin keeps a row only when POTA has NO number of its own for that part (KR.d9_winner of the record name over the state's other parks is None). Colorado: Great Sand Dunes Preserve US-8295's pin is inside the National Park record, but POTA numbers the park US-0033, so that record moves and nothing is asked; US-0033 / US-8295 each keep their own record (0 of 276 parks differ). Switch KPC_PRESERVE_APART, default ON. The states are those whose shapes hold an NPS record named Preserve.

changes.why: R-FJ1 (Fable's sheet, key-quality.md section 19 item 26; KPC owner 19 Nov 11:49 AM: 'yes pins are only references they are not always right'): a person's saved join may reach a record far from POTA's pin (past the 0.6 degree box) when the answer names that exact record id in both 'join' and 'far', carries decided_by and evidence (who, source, saw, date), and the record read today still fits its saved fingerprint (same name, acres within 10% or 20 ac). Never by name, never for a re-found id, never for an 'approx' answer, never past a NO. A far id that no longer fits goes to check; 'far' with no evidence is ignored. Switch KPC_FAR_JOIN, default ON. Only one answer carries 'far' today: Custer Gallatin NF US-4501 + PAD-US 2660 'Gallatin National Forest' (Montana).

changes.why: F10 (outside review, confirmed by a second checker; reviewer's go 19 Nov): an error inside the US key's one-record-two-parks pass (the kind pass, D9 and the contest) printed 'one-record-two-parks pass skipped' and the state was saved with its shared records in place. Behind the new switch KPC_HOLD_ON_PASS_ERROR (OFF): such an error holds the state the way any other error of a state does (run() fails, the builder names it FAILED, no key file is written and the state keeps its saved copy on main). No error = no change, switch on or off; merged OFF = the notice reads word for word as before. No result changes, nothing is rebuilt.
